27 Diagrams X and Y show the passage of water waves around an obstacle and through a gap.
The thick lines are barriers to the waves and each thin line represents a wavefront.
X
Y
Which statement is correct?
A
Diagrams X and Y both illustrate diffraction.
B
Diagrams X and Y both illustrate interference.
C
Only diagram X illustrates interference.
D
Only diagram Y illustrates diffraction.

hints: Look at what the thin lines do after the thick lines in each diagram - in X they curve around the ends of the obstacle and in Y they spread out in circles from the small gap.
Recall that diffraction is the spreading of a single wave into the shadow region when it passes an edge, obstacle or aperture of similar size to the wavelength.
Check for interference - it needs two coherent wave trains overlapping, but here there is only one incoming set of plane wavefronts in each diagram.
walkthrough: Identify the set-up: straight plane wavefronts arrive from the left in both diagrams. In X a thick vertical barrier blocks the middle, in Y a thick barrier with a small central gap blocks almost everything.
State the rule: diffraction is when waves pass an obstacle edge or narrow aperture and spread out into the geometrical shadow region, with wavefronts becoming curved.
Apply to Y: the thin lines change from straight to almost circular arcs centred on the gap, showing strong spreading through a gap of width similar to the wavelength.
Apply to X: the thin lines behind the barrier are also curved at the top and bottom edges, showing the wave bending around the obstacle into the region directly behind it.
Rule out interference: interference requires superposition of two or more coherent sources producing crossing patterns, but no second source or crossing pattern is present in either diagram.
Both diagrams therefore illustrate the same effect of spreading, so both illustrate diffraction. This is option A.

A.explanation: Both X with waves bending around the thick barrier and Y with waves spreading from the narrow gap show diffraction into the shadow region.

B.explanation: Interference needs two coherent sources overlapping to form maxima and minima, but each diagram shows only one set of spreading wavefronts.

C.explanation: Diagram X shows a single wave train bending around an obstacle, not two overlapping trains cancelling and reinforcing.

D.explanation: Diagram X also shows diffraction because the curved wavefronts behind the obstacle show spreading around its edges.
